events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $11.55 (model confidence 0.86)
events.body:
The trip ran 30.6 km against an optimal 22.4 km, a deviation of 8.19 km as billed [F1][F4]; that is well over the 1 km tolerance, so a refund is owed unless a segment is exempt [RD-1][RD-2]. The code also settled the traffic screen: the replaced stretch (Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway, band 2, 10–19 km/h) had a genuine traffic reason and no driver violation is recorded [F11][RD-4][RD-2]. A traffic reason does not reduce the amount; under RD-2 the refund turns only on whether the rider agreed to or asked for the route.

F3 (12:23–12:36, 7.52 km extra) is the only off-route segment, and the chat record is short and fully timestamped [F3][F9]. Before the segment the rider said only that she was waiting at the taxi stand in a grey hoodie [F7], and the driver replied he was on his way in a white BYD [F8]. Neither message names a road, area or place, and no rider message by 12:23:50 agrees to any reroute; the driver's "went round it" explanation appears only in his statement written after the trip, which is a claim and not prior consent [F10][RD-5]. So the ground is consent_after_or_none and the segment counts. The rider likewise named no stop, so no RD-3 exemption applies [F7][F8][RD-3].

Deviation: (8.19 km − 0 km exempt) × $1.4101/km = $11.55, matching the record's excess distance fare [F4][RD-2]. Tolls, time fare and surge are not refunded; surge is 1.0× so nothing is due under surge [F5][RD-2]. Under TH-1/TH-2 a route-deviation ruling of this size is made by the system, and the driver's clean profile (0 upheld, 0 disputes in 90 d) does not decide the case and triggers no repeat-offender flag [F17][RD-6]. The safety screen found nothing: the messages and complaint contain no threat, abuse or dangerous-driving allegation [F7][F8][F10][SAFE-1]. This follows the route-deviation precedent DISP-001, which refunded exactly the excess distance fare [PREC-1].
